caption:
Serendipity needs more than luck

In 1754, Horace Walpole read a Persian fairy tale about three princes who constantly made lucky discoveries. He used it to coin the word "serendipity."

The catch? Walpole said the princes found things they weren't looking for by accidents and sagacity. Luck was only part of it.

The payoff? Charles Goodyear dropped rubber mixed with sulfur on a hot frying pan in 1839. He noticed the rubber came out stronger and heat-resistant. Scientists stress that recognizing and acting on a chance is what counts. 🍀
